about.title: Moraga Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Moraga is a quiet Contra Costa County community of roughly 17,256 residents, but defective products don't discriminate by zip code — a faulty kitchen appliance, a poorly designed piece of yard equipment, or a mislabeled medication can hurt someone just as easily here as anywhere else. Under California law, injured people generally don't need to prove a manufacturer was careless; strict liability means showing the product itself was defective in design, manufacturing, or warning, and that the defect caused harm. That applies whether the company that made it, distributed it, or sold it is based nearby or across the country. If you or someone in your household was hurt by a product in or around Moraga, holding onto the item, its packaging, and any receipts matters. LawProactive is a free service that connects you with an independent attorney who can look at what happened and explain your options — no obligation, no law firm sales pitch from us.

whyChoose.title: Why Strict Liability Matters for Moraga Residents

items.title: You Don't Have to Prove Carelessness
items.desc: California's strict liability rule means the focus is on whether the product itself was defective, not whether the manufacturer was negligent. That can simplify what an injured person needs to show.

items.title: Multiple Parties May Share Responsibility
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and retailers can all potentially be held liable under strict liability, which widens who may be responsible for covering the harm caused.

items.title: Keeping the Product Preserves the Evidence
items.desc: Because the defect itself is central to the claim, holding onto the damaged product, packaging, and instructions can matter a great deal to how the case is evaluated.

items.question: Do I need to prove the manufacturer knew about the defect?
items.answer: Not necessarily. Under California's strict liability standard, the focus is generally on whether the product was defective and caused injury, not on what the manufacturer knew or intended. An independent attorney can review your situation to explain how this applies to your specific case.

items.question: What should I do with the product that hurt me?
items.answer: Try to preserve it exactly as it was at the time of the injury, along with any packaging, manuals, or receipts. Don't attempt repairs or throw it away, since the product itself is often central evidence in these claims.

items.question: Are product liability injuries common along roads like Moraga Road or Canyon Road?
items.answer: Product defects aren't limited to any particular street — they can involve household items, vehicles, or equipment used anywhere, including along busier Moraga corridors. If a vehicle part or equipment failure contributed to a crash or injury near these roads, it's worth having an independent attorney look into whether a product defect played a role.

items.question: Is there a cost to speak with an attorney through LawProactive?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service that connects injured people with independent attorneys who typically work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless there's a recovery. There's no obligation to move forward after speaking with one.
